# Draft:Herzegovina "Squeaking" Cheese

Herzegovina "Squeaking" Cheese (Bosnian: Škripavac) (Croatian: Škripavac) is a traditional fresh, soft, and full-fat cheese traditionally made from raw cow or sheep milk in Southern Herzegovina. It is named for the rubbery, squeaking sound it makes on the teeth when eaten fresh.
Origin:
Southern Herzegovina region, particularly around Trebinje, Ivanića, Slavogostići, and Gacko.
Production:
It is made by heating raw, fresh milk to roughly 37° C (98.6° F), then adding natural rennet, and then straining. Consumed young, often within days of production, as it is a fresh cheese with a short lifespan.
Texture and Taste:
It has a rubbery, springy, and squeaky texture and a milky, moderately salty, mild flavor.
Availability:
It is sold either directly by producers or found in open-air markets, such as the main square in Trebinje.
